title.narrative: I.1: % of young citizens who are very/fairly satisfied with the way democracy works in their country

description.narrative: I.1: % of young citizens who are very/fairly satisfied with the way democracy works in their country

comment.narrative: na
Increase in indicator

For 2021 the Afrobarometer showed 44.57 of young people satisfied with the way democracy works in their country this has decreased to 43.26 of young people expressing satisfaction for 2022 Afrobarometer 2022. In the Afrobarometer survey Round 9 20212023 60 of African youth aged 1835 expressed dissatisfaction with the way democracy works in their country. This dissatisfaction reflects broader concerns about the performance of democratic systems despite a preference for democracy over authoritarian forms of government. Afrobarometer found that youth are more critical of government performance particularly regarding unemployment and economic management. This is a sharp 326 decrease.The Latin American region generally reflects a mixed view on democracy among youth where political dissatisfaction is relatively high. Many young people feel disillusioned with the functioning of democracy in their countries with several expressing lower levels of trust in democratic institutions and governance. This sentiment is particularly strong among youth in countries facing economic hardship or political instability. According to LatinoBarmetro 2023 young people are more likely to express distrust in democratic institutions. For example the percentage of youth in countries like Argentina and Brazil expressing dissatisfaction with democracy is well above 50. In East and Southeast Asia younger citizens often display a more subdued commitment to liberal democracy compared to older generations. For instance Chinese youth tend to show higher satisfaction with the status quo and are less likely to engage in electoral or political activities than older cohorts. These trends reflect a generational decline in active political participation and a more pragmatic or limited view of democracy particularly in more authoritarian contexts like China. The report also highlights that youth in the region although they make up a significant portion of the population still face challenges in fully participating in democratic processes often due to both institutional barriers and limited opportunities for political engagementEach of these reports suggests a complex relationship between youth satisfaction and democratic governance. While young citizens in all three regions generally express a preference for democracy many are critical of its current performance particularly in terms of economic opportunities and political inclusion.

In addition to the 4 instances reported on in the previous interim report 1 September 2022 31 August 2023 below are 6 selected new instances out of a total of 8 new instances considered as cases of better collaboration YouthInAction campaign and Joint Statement for Summit for Democracy In the months of January to March 2024 ahead of the third Summit for Democracy the Youth Democracy Cohort launched a campaign titled YouthInAction which entailed collaborating on policy commentaries with activists and practitioners from the United States the Central African Republic Guyana and Australia. The campaign also concluded with the publication of a Joint Statement that was signed by 130 civil society organisations activists political parties young politicians and intergovernmental organisations. 3rd Summit for Democracy On 1820 March 2024 the Youth Democracy Cohort partnered closely with the National Endowment for Democracy to coordinate on the organisation of the Summit for Democracy in South Korea and push for greater youth representation in the event and as a topic. The YDC sent a delegation of 14 participants including partner organisations from the WYDE CE project. Club de Madrid Policy Lab From 1214 November 2023 in Brasilia the first inperson Policy Lab of the WYDE Network of Young DecisionMakers took place. 17 young decisionmakers participated in crafting concrete policy recommendations. The event included intergenerational dialogues and roundtable discussions with Club de Madrid Members fostering connections and enriching the discourse on global challenges. The EU Delegation in Brazil also participated adding valuable insights. This collaborative effort underscored the significance of intergenerational dialogue and culminated in actionable strategies presented during the Club de Madrid Annual Policy Dialogue at Itamaraty shaping the WG Papers and the final outcome document to guide actions on pressing global issues. Alma Civica collaboration with BYAN On 28 September 2023 the Blind Youth Association of Nepal BYAN had a meeting with Alma Civica from Paraguay to present each others work exchange ideas and resources around civic education programmes. Accountability Hubs collaboration Throughout the reporting period the 20 young leaders members of the Accountability Hubs 202324 of the Kofi Annan Foundation one francophone hub for West Africa and one anglophone hub have established strong crossborder collaboration working jointly to come up with innovative project ideas to address challenges to democracy and accountable governance in their countries and communities in SubSaharan Africa. Youth Democracy Cohort and Accountability Lab On 23 May 2024 the European Partnership and Accountability Lab signed a Memorandum of Understanding MoU to enhance their collaboration to advance youth political participation through the Youth Democracy Cohort and the Open Government Partnership.

The following five cases are a sample of the 18 new cases that occurred during the reporting period. The complete list is not provided here as several of these cases showcase the same outcome. For example the Uganda Democracy Academy comforted several alumni to run for offices as it did for Ikyriza Gold. The five cases showcased below provide a good indication of what all 18 cases managed to achieve.Alma Civica An active participant of Alma Civica subgranted project demonstrated his commitment by coordinating a group of volunteers to implement the survey planned in the project.Impressed by the work done on the project the participant then invited Alma Civica to hold a civic workshop for 33 students of the National College Sacred Heart of Jesus located in the city of R.I. 3 Corrales in the department of Caaguaz and supported in the management of the workshop to expand opportunities for civic development to young people in his community. Uganda Democracy Academy During the Uganda Students Association UNSA campaigns in November 2023 graduates of the Uganda Democracy Academy donated money to support the campaign of fellow alumni Ikyriza Gold who was running for Vice President. Federation of Liberian Youth FLY Following the post elections town hall organised in December 2023 by FLY young people shifted from a behaviour of aggressiveness personal attacks and fights before the meeting to apologising shaking hands and hugging during the meeting. This happened especially in Nimba county where tensions are usually high and where a football tournament and other community activities were organised. Alumni of UDA By March 2024 within 6 months of the completion of the Uganda Democracy Academy five alumni expressed interest in running for elective positions in the next Ugandan general elections in 2026. Decidamos On 18 March 2024 Decidamos with the group Presencia Joven managed to have a public audience with the secretary of youth of the department of Itapua to discuss their views and push for specific demands. The meeting came from an advocacy campaign on the topic of mental health which they also chose independently of the youth from Central in collaboration with five local organisations Universitarias Feministas de Itapa Kua Roga Kua Sorora Diversxs Encarnacin y La Poderosa Paraguay.

The following 5 cases are a sample of the 7 new instances that happened during Year 2 of the action. They show the impact measures in the different countries and offer a representative sample of what the project achieved so far Youth Legislative Caucus in Liberia The House of Representatives adopted the Youth Legislative Caucus on 12 March 2024 after a number of background conversations with law makers. The Caucus will henceforth advocate for Youth Development policies and advocate for youth inclusion on participation and decision making from the level of the Legislature. They will help to Facilitate the implementation of the Youth Impact Monitoring and Assessment. Youth engagement in Nepal In 2024 the municipal government of Pokhara in Nepal reactivated the Municipal Youth Council engaging with young people and ensuring their input in policy making. Youth representation in Nigeria The president named a 78yearold man as Youth Minister. Brain Builders EPDs partner supported through the Youth Democracy Cohort subgrants advocated for a change in the nomination. A few weeks later a 37 years old woman was nominated instead. Youth consultation in Paraguay The Director General of the Cabinet of the Governors Office of the Central region Gloria Rodrguez announced her willingness to sign a framework agreement for cooperation with the Decidamos citizen observation network during the advocacy meeting on 14 February 2024. The Head of the Secretariat of Equity Gender and Human Development Laura Moreira the Head of the Youth Area Rodrigo Rodrguez and the Head of the Womens Area Mara Elena Bentez also attended the meeting and listened to the youth organisation proposals. Youth Bill in Zimbabwe In July 2023 the Zimbabwe Amendment Number 2 Bill introduced the Youth quota which resulted in the creation of 10 parliamentary seats reserved exclusively for youth aged between 21 and 35. Gwen Trust worked with other youthled organisations to lobby the government to achieve this result.
